findings.title: Fragile string-based resolution of the English reference file
findings.body: The English counterpart file is located by doing a plain string replace on the absolute path (`resources-community`→`resources`, then `_<locale>.properties`→`_en.properties`). This assumes every verified properties file lives in a `resources`/`resources-community` theme tree with a sibling `_en.properties` file following exactly this naming convention. If a file doesn't match this pattern (e.g. is not itself under one of these two trees, has a differently-formed locale suffix, or has no English counterpart at all), `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` will throw `FileNotFoundException`, which is wrapped in a `RuntimeException` (see line 78-79) instead of a clear Maven error. This makes the verifier brittle to any directory/naming variation and produces a confusing stack trace rather than an actionable build failure.

findings.title: Unchecked RuntimeException bypasses the MojoExecutionException contract
findings.body: verify() declares `throws MojoExecutionException` and only catches `IOException` around the call to `verifySafeHtml()`. However, `verifySafeHtml()` wraps any IOException it encounters (e.g. missing English file, line 70 and 78-79) in an unchecked `RuntimeException`, which is not caught by the `catch (IOException e)` in `verify()`. As a result, any failure while reading the referenced English file propagates out of `verify()` as a raw RuntimeException, bypassing the plugin's intended error-reporting path and surfacing as an unhandled exception in the Maven build instead of a clean, actionable error message.

findings.title: Hard-coded, non-extensible whitelist for MessageFormat choice/placeholder exceptions
findings.body: normalizeValue() special-cases only four specific keys (`templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, keys starting with `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit`, and `error-invalid-multivalued-size`) to strip angle-bracket placeholders or MessageFormat `{n,choice,...}` syntax that would otherwise be mistaken for HTML by the sanitizer. Any future message key that introduces similar `{n,choice,...}` syntax or literal `<...>` placeholder text (as several locale files in this very PR needed, e.g. `error-invalid-multivalued-size` in multiple languages) will not be covered by this list and will cause false 'Illegal HTML' failures until someone manually extends this hard-coded list. There is no generic handling of MessageFormat choice syntax across all keys, only for the enumerated ones.

findings.title: No positive-path tests for the new HTML/anchor sanitizer
findings.body:
All four new/updated tests (`verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected`, `verifyNoHtmlAllowed`, `verifyNoChangedAnchors`, and the duplicate-key test) only assert that violations are correctly detected. There is no test confirming that a translation containing legitimate HTML matching the English source (e.g. matching ``/``/`

` tags in both English and translation) passes verification without any findings. Given the complexity of the anchor-matching and choice-format normalization logic in `VerifyMessageProperties`, lacking a 'happy path' regression test risks silently breaking valid translations in the future without any test failing.

findings.title: New dependency versions hard-coded instead of using property placeholders
findings.body: The newly added `owasp-java-html-sanitizer` (20240325.1) and `commons-text` (1.13.0) dependencies have their versions hard-coded inline, while every other dependency in this pom (maven-plugin-api, maven-plugin-tools, etc.) uses a `<properties>`-defined version variable. This is inconsistent with the existing convention in the file and makes future version bumps/dependency management (e.g. via a BOM) harder to track centrally.
